name: cloud_native_voucher_medium
description: Synthetic medium-sized Docker-on-VM voucher management service inspired by the domain and requirements-document scale of PURE's Voucher Management System. No PURE requirement sentence is reproduced.

source.referenceTitle: Software Requirements Specification for Voucher Management System
source.synthesisMethod: Use the public document's domain and SRS-style requirement granularity, then author new cloud-native requirements for a Docker-on-VM experiment.
source.citation: Ferrari, Spagnolo, Gnesi. PURE: A Dataset of Public Requirements Documents. RE'17, pp. 502-505. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.7118517.

resource_constraints_text: Deploy the Docker-based service to Azure Korea Central on Linux VMs. The monthly infrastructure budget is at most 600 USD. At least 4 vCPUs are required. Traffic is spiky, with campaign launches causing short peaks. A single availability zone is acceptable for this experiment.

classified.text: Issuer administrators create voucher campaigns with a name, active period, and total issuance limit.
Issuer administrators define each campaign's voucher value, eligibility conditions, and redemption rules.
Issuer administrators import eligible recipients and receive a report of accepted and rejected records.
The system issues a unique voucher to each eligible recipient without exceeding the campaign limit.
Recipients retrieve their active, redeemed, and expired vouchers.
Merchant operators validate a voucher before accepting a purchase.
Merchant operators redeem a valid voucher for an eligible purchase.
The system rejects a second redemption of a voucher that has already been redeemed.
Authorized issuer administrators reverse an erroneous redemption and record the reason.
The system marks vouchers as expired after their campaign validity period ends.
Issuer administrators suspend and resume voucher campaigns.
Support agents search voucher issuance and redemption history by voucher, campaign, recipient, merchant, and time range.
Issuer administrators request a campaign report containing issuance, redemption, reversal, and expiration totals.
The system exports a requested campaign report as a downloadable file.
The system notifies recipients when vouchers are issued, redeemed, reversed, or close to expiration.
External issuer systems receive signed webhook events for voucher lifecycle changes.
All external API traffic must use HTTPS.
Voucher, campaign, recipient, and redemption records must remain durable across application and VM restarts.
Concurrent redemption attempts for the same voucher must produce at most one successful redemption.
The voucher validation API must respond within 500 milliseconds at the 95th percentile under 50 requests per second.
The service must support short traffic peaks of 200 requests per second during campaign launches.
Application processes must remain stateless so that any running instance can handle an API request.
Webhook delivery must retry transient failures and retain undelivered events for 24 hours.
Administrative changes and voucher lifecycle transitions must produce audit records retained for one year.
Credentials, signing keys, and database passwords must be supplied at runtime and must not be stored in the application image.
The service must emit structured logs and expose health and request-latency metrics.
Campaign report files must remain downloadable for 30 days after generation.
The application must be packaged as a Docker image and run on Linux virtual machines.
